name: Bonus
authority: CPF Act 1953 First Schedule: a bonus is an Additional Wage, charged under the Additional Wage ceiling (102,000 less the year’s Ordinary Wages subject to CPF).

name: Salary in lieu of notice
authority: Employment Act 1968 s.11(1): either party may end the contract without notice by paying the salary at the gross rate of pay that would have accrued over the notice period (s.10(3), where the contract states none: one day under 26 weeks' service, one week under two years, two weeks under five, four weeks from five); raised by HR with the amount, since MOM states no formula for a monthly-rated employee's week. CPF Board (“Are CPF contributions payable on compensation in lieu of notice?”; Refund Reasons: salary in lieu of notice does not attract CPF): outside CPF. The self-help group funds follow the CPF base, so it is outside CDAC, ECF, MBMF and SINDA: CPF Board FAQ “Are CPF contributions payable on compensation in lieu of notice?” — “CPF contributions are not payable on compensation in lieu of notice payable by you to your employee”; CPF Board FAQ on SHG contributions for 13th month wage — they are “based on the total wages payable to an employee in a calendar month”; CPF Board FAQ on interns — CDAC, ECF and SINDA contributions “are payable … if CPF contributions are payable” (the CDAC Rules (CPFA1953-R6) r.3(1) deduct “from the monthly wages” at the Schedule rate and define no wages of their own, so Interpretation Act 1965 s.21 — “expressions used in the subsidiary legislation have the same meanings as in the Act conferring the power” — gives the term its CPF Act 1953 s.2(1) meaning, “the remuneration in money, including any bonus, due or granted to a person in respect of the person’s employment”; citations verified on sso.agc.gov.sg 2026-09-23, round 5); Muis, MBMF employer information, Table 2: “Termination Benefits — Retirement gratuity, retrenchment pay, ex-gratia payment, salary in lieu of notice, severance pay, compensation for loss of employment” — Accounted for MBMF: No. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.2: “wages” is the remuneration in money due in respect of the employment, and the only payments notified out of it are medical reimbursements (S 375/2023), so it counts toward SDL.

name: Retrenchment benefit
authority: Employment Act 1968 s.45: no employee with under 2 years’ continuous service is entitled to a retrenchment benefit, and no provision fixes a quantum for longer service; a contractual or negotiated retrenchment benefit is raised by HR with the amount. CPF Board (“Are CPF contributions payable on redundancy payment?”): “CPF contributions are not payable on termination benefits given for retrenchment or loss of employment”, so it is outside CPF and, following the CPF base, outside CDAC, ECF and SINDA; Muis, MBMF employer information, Table 2: retrenchment pay — Accounted for MBMF: No. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.2 (read on sso.agc.gov.sg, current version as at 28 Sep 2026): “wages” means “the remuneration in money, including any bonus, due or granted to a person in respect of the person’s employment but does not include such payments as the Minister may, by notification in the Gazette, specify”; the only notified exclusion is medical, dental and TCM reimbursement (S 375/2023), and no SDL or Agency publication addresses retrenchment pay. Owner rule 2026-09-28: law silent on this payment; default counts toward SDL, read as SALARY_IN_LIEU_OF_NOTICE is (the same s.2 words); lawful because SDL is employer-borne, s.3(2) caps it at 0.25% of $4,500 a month, and any excess is refundable under SDL Regulations reg.13, whereas the other reading risks an Agency assessment for unpaid levy. IRAS: compensation for loss of employment is not taxable and is reported apart from gratuity, notice pay and ex-gratia (Form IR8A item d3, Explanatory Notes YA 2027).

name: Damage or loss recovery
authority: EA s.29 and MOM salary-deductions guidance: one-time recovery only after an inquiry and an opportunity to explain; input amount must be the evidenced actual loss attributable to the employee. Payroll enforces the independent quarter-month salary limit. Do not split one loss into repeated requests.

name: Accommodation recovery
authority: EA s.30 and MOM salary-deductions guidance: input amount must not exceed the value of accommodation supplied and accepted by the employee; retain acceptance and valuation evidence. Payroll caps accommodation plus amenities/services at a quarter of salary for the salary period.

name: Amenities or services recovery
authority: EA s.30 and MOM salary-deductions guidance: input amount must not exceed the value of accepted amenities/services authorised by the Commissioner for Labour; retain permission, acceptance and valuation evidence. Payroll caps accommodation plus amenities/services at a quarter of salary for the salary period.

name: Registered co-operative dues
authority: EA ss.27(1)(j),32(1): payment to a registered co-operative society with the employee written consent is outside the aggregate 50% limit. Input amount and evidence identify the consented subscription, entrance fee, loan instalment, interest or other due. This is not an employer loan.

name: Commissioner-approved damage recovery
authority: Employment Act 1968 s.29(1): the quarter-month limit may be exceeded with the Commissioner permission. Input amount must be within the evidenced actual loss and the permission, following an inquiry and opportunity to explain; attach that permission to this one-time request. Payroll still enforces the s.32 aggregate salary-period limit except on final salary. https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968?WholeDoc=1
